note: What the creatures do, the routes through this place, and what a Remix may change.

locked: Core problem: Protective wards misfire and corrupted creatures threaten the settlement.
Moral question: protect the village immediately, preserve evidence, or pursue the source before the crisis worsens.
open: The crabs came when the harbor ward-stone's light faltered; its light leans uphill toward the buried watch-temple (VI-HB-02).
Villagers shelter with Lira in the net store (VI-HB-03); someone is still missing on the quay.
Rusk's Unrepentant rides at the pier's end, its gangplank hauled in: no one boards without a fare.

After the fight Tovan the blacksmith presses a fist-sized, star-flecked lump of black forge-stone on the champion: 'Keep the road honest.' He can't say where it came from; it was on his anvil block when he inherited the forge. It is the stone the road forge's wheel needs in chapter 2.

original.does: Heaves out of the harbor along the quay and the pier, shells glowing blue at the joints where the misfiring ward touched them; grabs whoever is nearest and drags them toward the water.

difficulty.tuner_recommends: as built (plays as moderate); not applied unless the map says so

terrain.water: the harbor along the quay and around the pier; deep water off the pier's end
rewards: creatures that climb out of water
grapplers that pull characters to the edge
terrain.gaps: the lane and the boathouse door are 5 ft; the quay is open

may_change: the read-aloud and GM lines about them
must_keep: creatures from the sea, corrupted by the misfiring ward (the faint blue glow)
the ward-stone plaza's leaning light as the clue to the watch-temple
villagers in danger, so that acting now matters

filters.movement: swimmers that can climb onto the quay fit best

remix.freshness: a remix for returning players avoids Giant Crabs (the watch-temple's breach has them too)

routes.when: A character reaches the ward-stone plaza (VI-HB-02) while the crabs are on the quay.
routes.success: The character gets several villagers to stand together by the stone instead of fleeing: its light steadies, and the crabs flinch from it and slide back into the harbor. Only those already grappling someone fight on.
routes.failure: One frightened voice shouts everyone back indoors; the stone stutters and the crabs come on as written.
routes.reveals: The stone answers many people choosing the same thing, and falters when one voice decides for all. Describe it; never explain it.
routes.canon: A fair-play clue for the GM-only truth about the village, shown and not told; it also answers the moral question by protecting the village first.

routes.when: Anyone near the fish market stalls or the boathouse, where the day's catch lies gutted.
routes.success: Buckets of offal tipped off the far end of the quay draw the crabs away from the people: they join the fight only from the third round, and only if someone stays on the quay.
routes.failure: The crabs turn on the bucket-bearer and close at once.
routes.reveals: Nothing new: the crabs are only hungry, and wrong.
routes.canon: Protects the villagers without solving the source: the watch-temple still waits.

routes.when: A character hails the Unrepentant from the pier.
routes.condition: A fare Rusk accepts (coin, a favour owed, or a promise he can collect on). Rusk never names his price during the danger.
routes.success: Rusk's crew drop a net and boathooks over the side: the crabs on the pier are pinned and pushed back into the water. Rusk names his price later, and expects it paid.
routes.failure: Rusk shrugs: 'No fare, no favour.' The fight runs as written.
routes.cost: A debt to Brannoc Rusk, collected in a later chapter.
routes.reveals: Rusk: 'A fare accepted is a life entrusted. A fare refused is your own business.'
routes.canon: Establishes Rusk's narrow code (Freedom Without Virtue) at the party's first meeting.
